name: Meridian Munitions Coach-12 'Stagecoach'
description:
The Meridian Munitions Coach-12 is a break-action side-by-side shotgun chambered in 12 gauge, featuring two 18-inch barrels, exposed hammers, and a wooden stock that would not have been out of place two centuries ago. The weapon holds exactly two rounds, fires them as fast as the shooter can pull the dual triggers, and reloads by breaking the action open and dropping in fresh shells.

The Stagecoach is an anachronism that refuses to die. It is mechanically the simplest possible shotgun — no magazine tube, no gas system, no pump mechanism. Two barrels, two hammers, two triggers. The break action means the weapon can be loaded, stored, and verified at a glance. Nothing can go wrong mechanically that a hinge pin replacement won't fix. This radical simplicity keeps the Stagecoach in production despite being technically obsolete by two centuries.

Meridian Munitions sells the Coach-12 for less than most pump-action shotguns, and it finds buyers among residents who value simplicity above all else. Elderly Shelf residents, rural settlers, and individuals with physical limitations that make pump-action or semi-automatic operation difficult all gravitate toward the Stagecoach. Two rounds of 12-gauge buckshot at close range remains devastatingly effective, and the weapon's limitations are irrelevant if the encounter ends in two shots.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 25 meters (buckshot)
rate_of_fire: Two shots (break-action reload)
magazine_capacity: 2 rounds
weight: 2.6 kg
tactical_use: A minimal-capacity close-range shotgun offering extreme simplicity at the cost of capacity and reload speed. Both barrels can be fired in rapid succession for a devastating two-shot volley. Reloading requires opening the break action and inserting fresh shells individually. Not suitable for any engagement requiring more than two shots. Best deployed as an ambush or first-contact defensive weapon.
cultural_context: The Stagecoach is beloved by people who distrust complexity. In Shelf culture, it occupies a position of folksy respect — the weapon your grandparent kept by the door, and their grandparent before them. The break-action shotgun is so culturally embedded that it transcends the firearms debate entirely; even anti-weapons advocates struggle to argue against something so plainly defensive and limited.
story_hooks: A Stagecoach loaded with two rounds of slug is the only weapon available when a group of people need to hold a door against multiple attackers. The math is terrible, but the courage isn't.
An antique Stagecoach is discovered with custom-loaded shells sealed in the chamber for decades. Whatever is in those shells, it isn't standard ammunition.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately retro side-by-side shotgun with an aggressive, compact stance. Twin barrels dominate the profile, flared slightly at the muzzles. Exposed hammer spurs rise above the receiver like predatory ears. The wooden furniture evokes 19th-century craftsmanship, yet the precise metalwork and tight tolerances scream modern manufacturing. A weapon that looks both timeless and deliberately defiant against trend.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 112 cm | Barrel length: 46 cm | Width across barrels at muzzle: 4.2 cm | Stock length of pull: 36 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced. The 2.6 kg distributes naturally between the barrels and stock, encouraging shouldering. Not light, but purposeful—every gram serves function.
physical_description.primary_material: Blued steel receiver and barrels; walnut or walnut-grain composite stock and fore-end. Steel trigger assembly with hardened sear components.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte blue on all steel surfaces—not glossy, but rich and absorptive. The wood finish is satin, revealing natural grain without artifice. Minimal cosmetic polish; emphasis on durability over shine.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal blue-black as primary | Natural walnut brown as secondary | Brushed steel on trigger guards and hammer spurs as accent
physical_description.grip_texture: Walnut stock with traditional checkering pattern cut into pistol grip and fore-end—fine crosshatch texture for secure purchase even with gloved hands. Slightly raised comb. Warm wood feel contrasts with cool steel trigger assembly.
distinctive_features: Dual exposed hammer spurs with pronounced knurling for thumb-cocking
Break-action hinge pin visible on right side of receiver
Twin trigger assembly: front trigger fires right barrel, rear trigger fires left barrel
Simple bead front sight on top rib
Ejector pods on breech face—bright metal showing when action opens
Minimal safety lever (if present) integrated into trigger guard
No rails, no optics mounts, no accessory points
Faint manufacturing witness marks on barrel flats
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS stamped in serif font on top rib between barrels. Serial number etched on left side of receiver. COACH-12 marked on barrel flat. '12 GA' stamped on breech face. Simple blocky logo—no elaborate branding.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show honest wear: scuffed wood from sling swivels or holster contact, light patina on steel surfaces (not rust, but honest oxidation), possible handling marks on receiver. Mechanically pristine—these weapons are maintained religiously by owners who understand simplicity equals reliability. Never tacticool, never cosmetically modified. Functional beauty.
